the_read: BG3 is in settled-classic mode at 27 months post-launch: $760M lifetime revenue, 21M owners, and a 7-day revenue delta of +0.2% means the tail is flat but still printing. Larian's leverage here is catalogue-economics, not new-user acquisition.

The 4.43M residual wishlist pile is the headline anomaly. That is a wishlist book larger than most AAA launches ever achieve, sitting on a 2-year-old SKU. It implies a structural conversion drip at every seasonal sale and a coiled spring for any console-version port refresh or definitive-edition repackage.

Attention signals have decayed to maintenance levels (1,910 concurrent Twitch viewers, 25 to 100 stream count) which is exactly what you want at this lifecycle stage — no marketing spend, organic floor intact, 97% positive across 838K reviews. The unit economics now favor mod tooling investment and a Definitive Edition SKU over a sequel rush.
1086940.against_consensus: Consensus treats BG3 as the genre's high-water mark and Larian's next move as the only question. The contrarian read: the 4.4M wishlist overhang is worth more than most people model, because CRPG buyers are notoriously sale-elastic. A 75%-off Steam event on this title moves more incremental gross than a mid-tier publisher's full-price Q4 release. Larian's most valuable asset right now might be patience.
1086940.comparable: Closest analogue is Skyrim (2011), which at a comparable 24-month mark was still riding mod-ecosystem cohort renewal toward what became a 287K peak CCU and a 15-year tail. BG3's projected settled band of 210K–420K peak CCU sits roughly 25% above Skyrim's peak, but Skyrim's lifetime unit count is roughly 1.5× BG3's current 21M — the gap closes only if Larian ships official mod tooling parity.
1086940.what_would_change_my_mind: If the 4.43M wishlist count fails to convert meaningfully (under 8% conversion) during the next two major Steam sales, the residual-demand thesis collapses and BG3 becomes a flat-tail asset rather than a compounding one.
risks: Larian's stated pivot away from D&D caps franchise compounding optionality.
CRPG TAM ceiling means scale band is genuinely settled, not latent.
1086940.pull_quote: A 4.4M wishlist book on a two-year-old SKU is a coiled spring, not a leftover.

the_read: R.E.P.O. has already cleared the cult threshold by an order of magnitude: 21.5M owners, $143.8M lifetime revenue at a $9.99 SKU, and 386K reviews at 96% positive. The 'Cult 8-25K CCU' band in the scorecard is stale — this is a phenom that's now in its tail-management phase, not its discovery phase.

The interesting signal this week is the wishlist stack: 1.47M wishlists post-launch is not a discovery queue, it's a price-sensitivity reservoir waiting on the first meaningful discount or 1.0 transition. Twitch at 2.3K CCV with streams doubling 55→100 suggests a small second-wave cresting, not a fresh cascade.

Unit economics are already settled. At ~$143M gross on a four-person studio, the question for buy-side is no longer whether R.E.P.O. works — it's whether semiwork can convert the audience into a second SKU or a 1.0 monetization event without fumbling the goodwill.
3241660.against_consensus: Consensus still files R.E.P.O. under 'current breakout.' The numbers say it's already broken out and the relevant question is decay curve management. Revenue 7d delta of +0.5% is the tell — this is a mature EA asset coasting on installed base, not an accelerating one. Pricing the studio's next move matters more than tracking this week's Twitch chart.
3241660.comparable: Lethal Company peaked at 250K CCU on a similar streamable-coop-under-$10 configuration. R.E.P.O. is running a different shape: lower CCU ceiling but a much wider owner base at 21.5M versus Lethal Company's roughly 15M, a gap of about 6.5M owners in R.E.P.O.'s favor. The Friendslop cluster monetizes breadth over concurrency, and R.E.P.O. is the cleanest current example.
3241660.what_would_change_my_mind: If the 1.0 release lands without a meaningful CCU spike above the EA peak, the thesis that 1.47M wishlists represent a real conversion reservoir is falsified.

3241660.pull_quote: 1.47M wishlists post-launch isn't a discovery queue, it's a price-sensitivity reservoir waiting on the first meaningful discount.

the_read: Lifetime revenue of $581M on 17.4M owners puts Wukong inside the top five Chinese-developed PC launches ever, but the week-over-week revenue delta of +0.1% confirms what the Twitch read (273 CCV across 55 streams) already says: the tail is normalizing and the front-loaded curve is what it is.

Wishlist stock of 4.81M is the headline metric being misread. That's a conversion overhang, not future demand — most of those were stacked pre-launch and the ~17.4M owners suggest the easy conversions have already triggered. Discount elasticity, not new cohort capture, is the lever from here.

On unit economics this is already a returned bet many times over. The interesting question for buy-side is whether Game Science behaves like FromSoft (15-year IP compounder) or like a one-shot studio milking the catalog. No DLC roadmap announced is the tell worth tracking.
2358720.against_consensus: Consensus still files Wukong under active breakout. It isn't — it's a settled hit with a 97% review score and a flat revenue line. The second wave needs a DLC trigger, and there isn't one on the board.

Wukong is at $581M and 17.4M owners on a comparable timeline — higher unit count, lower revenue capture per unit (price + regional mix), and Twitch CCV of 273 versus Elden Ring's ~80K. 2358720.what_would_change_my_mind: A dated DLC or expansion announcement with a Steam page would reset the wishlist stock into actual forward intent and re-open the breakout argument.

2358720.pull_quote: Wishlist stock of 4.81M is a conversion overhang, not future demand.

149K concurrent Twitch viewers against 99 streams is a thin creator base relative to audience appetite — a viewership-to-streamer ratio over 1,500:1 typically signals demand outstripping content supply, which is the inverse of the Marvel's Avengers attention shape.

77% positive on 387K reviews is the structural watch-point. Hero-shooters historically need the high 70s to clear the six-month live-service hurdle; Overwatch 2 launched at 18% on Steam and never recovered the cohort, so Rivals having survived the first patch cycle without sentiment collapse matters more than the raw CCU.

The gap is structural loop design, not marketing spend.
2767030.what_would_change_my_mind: If season two retention shows a week-3 cohort drop exceeding 40% against season one's baseline, the Avengers comparison reactivates.

Wishlist tail at 2.15M post-launch is the number to watch: that is conversion overhang, not pre-launch intent. People are buying in waves as friends form squads, which is the Friendslop signature rather than the Soulslike one.

Attention has cooled hard. Twitch at 913 CCV with 99 streams is cult-band territory, and the +0.4% revenue delta says the launch spike is over. The question is whether this settles as a $150M one-and-done or compounds via patches and a DLC roadmap FromSoft has not historically run.
2622380.against_consensus: Consensus is reading Nightreign as a disappointment against Elden Ring's shadow. The business read is different: a $40 derivative project shipping 3M units with 82% positive on a format FromSoft has never attempted before is a strong portfolio outcome for Bandai Namco. 2622380.comparable: Elden Ring (2022) was doing 953K peak CCU and dominating Twitch front-page at the equivalent post-launch window. 2622380.what_would_change_my_mind: A patch or content drop that pushes Twitch CCV back above 5,000 sustained for a week would signal genuine multiplayer compounding rather than a fading launch tail.

2622380.pull_quote: Stop benchmarking a $40 derivative against the mainline — 3M units on an experiment is a portfolio win, not a miss.

the_read: Khazan has done $26.3M lifetime against 736K owners at $59.99 — a credible mid-tier soulslike result for Neople, but the 1.40M wishlist stockpile at launch implied a much larger conversion than the install base suggests. Roughly 53% wishlist conversion is fine; it is not the cohort capture the wishlist count was pricing in.

The signal mix is lopsided: intent and community fired hard (89K followers, 16K subreddit, 1.4M wishlists), but attention has collapsed post-launch to 95 concurrent Twitch viewers across 14 streams. That is a single-player narrative soulslike behaving exactly as the category dictates — front-loaded sales, no streamer tail, no second wind.

Unit economics still work. 85% positive across 30.5K reviews is healthy for the subgenre, and a Nexon-adjacent publisher with DNF Duel/Dungeon Fighter infrastructure absorbs marketing cost differently than an indie would. The commercial question is whether DLC or a New Game+ content drop can reactivate the wishlist residual that did not convert at launch.
2680010.against_consensus: Consensus reads Khazan as a quiet win because reviews are positive and it shipped clean. The business read is more cautious: a 1.4M wishlist game converting to roughly 737K owners is underperforming its own pre-launch intent curve, and the attention signals say the discovery window has closed. This is a respectable mid-tier outcome, not a sleeper trajectory.
2680010.comparable: Hades (2020) at a comparable post-launch window was running ~49K peak CCU on a $24.99 narrative product with critical-phenom positioning, monetizing via awards-driven retention. Khazan projects to 1K–6K peak CCU at $59.99 — a roughly 10–50× CCU gap, though ARPU is roughly 2.4× higher. Different category math entirely, but the EA-to-retention playbook is not available to Khazan as a launched single-player product.
2680010.what_would_change_my_mind: A paid DLC or substantive content patch within six months driving a sustained 3×-plus CCU rebound and renewed press cycle would reframe this as a platform rather than a one-shot.

2680010.pull_quote: A 1.4M wishlist game converting to 737K owners is a respectable mid-tier outcome, not a sleeper trajectory.

the_read: Palworld at 19.6M owners and $394M lifetime revenue is not a breakout candidate — it is a post-breakout asset cooling into its long tail, with revenue 7d delta at +0.1% and Twitch live viewers at 348.

The interesting datapoint is the streams count moving 29 to 78 week-over-week against flat viewership. That is creator-side speculation, not audience-side demand, and historically precedes a content drop or a Pocketpair PR beat rather than organic resurgence.

Wishlists holding at 2.59M this deep into EA is the genuinely unusual reading here. Conversion has already happened for the core cohort, so that pool is either 1.0 vs 1.1 patch waiters or a free-weekend lever Pocketpair hasn't pulled yet.

1623730.comparable: Lethal Company peaked near 250K CCU on a sub-$10 SKU with a solo dev and zero wishlist runway. 1623730.what_would_change_my_mind: A major content drop or 1.0 announcement that pushes Twitch concurrents above 25,000 and converts more than 200,000 of the standing wishlist pool within two weeks.

the_read: Silksong shipped 5.6M units and $82.6M lifetime revenue at $19.99 in roughly twelve weeks, off a 3.29M wishlist book that accumulated across a six-year wait — the cleanest conversion of a pre-launch intent stockpile we've logged this cycle.

Attention is where the thesis gets uncomfortable: 1,528 concurrent Twitch viewers and 97 active streams put it well below the streamer-retention threshold metroidvanias need for a long tail, and the +0.3% revenue delta this week says the launch cohort has already been served.

Unit economics remain the story. Team Cherry is three people on a self-published title with no publisher rev-share drag — at 89% positive across 406K reviews, contribution margin on every marginal unit is structurally higher than anything a publisher-funded comp can match, which lets the tail compound at low absolute volume.
Projected peak CCU sits in the 1K–6K Watch band, which is the correct read for a launched product 12 weeks in, not a verdict on the title's quality.
1030300.against_consensus: Consensus treats Silksong as a generational success and stops there. The numerate read is that the IP did the work the product now has to defend — attention metrics have already normalized to indie-mid levels, and the question for anyone modeling Team Cherry's next move is whether a six-year gap recurs or whether the studio scales. Those are different businesses.
1030300.comparable: Closest analog is Hades (2020): at the equivalent post-1.0 window Supergiant was running ~25K peak CCU sustained by awards-cycle coverage and EA-cohort word-of-mouth. Silksong's current 1,528 Twitch viewers and Watch-band CCU projection sit roughly 15-20x below where Hades was building its month-2-onwards retention curve, despite Silksong's lifetime revenue already exceeding Hades' first-year haul by a wide margin.
1030300.what_would_change_my_mind: If Twitch concurrents re-accelerate above 5,000 on a content patch or DLC drop within six months, the tail thesis flips from decay to compounding.
risks: Wishlist book is spent; no second intent reservoir behind it.

Unit economics here are obscene. Solo dev, no publisher, Steam's 70% cut on ~$130M gross translates to roughly $90M+ net to TVGS before tax. The 1.73M wishlist overhang is the asset to underwrite — that is a 1.0 launch detonator most Hooded Horse or Devolver titles would underwrite a sequel against.

Where it gets interesting commercially: 3.4M wishlists still sitting on the books after launch. That is conversion ammunition for the awards-season push and any subsequent content drop. Supergiant has historically monetized post-launch narrative beats and TGA cycles better than they monetize launch week.

Buy-side modelling a linear ramp from here is mispricing the curve.
1145350.comparable: Hades (2020) hit roughly 49K peak CCU on 1.0 launch and converted EA goodwill into a critical-phenom run that durably compounded via awards coverage. 1145350.pull_quote: Supergiant has historically monetized post-launch narrative beats and TGA cycles better than they monetize launch week.

the_read: Halo Infinite is a four-year-old F2P shooter sitting on $104M lifetime revenue and 18.8M owners, with a 7-day revenue delta of +0.1% — this is not a breakout, it is a flat ambient base catching a Twitch ripple of 12.3K CLV off 70 streams.

The intent signals (312K wishlists, 230K followers) are stock, not flow — accumulated over a multi-year tail, not a fresh demand spike. Wishlist on an already-launched F2P title is a near-meaningless number that the breakout score is over-weighting.

69% positive across 180K reviews is the structural ceiling here. The economics of a Microsoft-funded live-service flagship mean Infinite doesn't need to break out to justify itself internally, but for outside capital there is no ride to buy — the float is owned by Xbox and the upside is capped by a loop the market has already priced.
1240440.against_consensus: Consensus treats every Halo Twitch flicker as a potential revival arc. The contrarian read: Infinite's curve is a flat utility, not a coiled spring. Each season cycle produces a 10-14 day attention bump that decays to baseline. The +22 score delta is noise on a low base, not the front edge of a Lethal Company-style cascade.
1240440.comparable: Closest analog is Marvel's Avengers — an IP-led live-service that mistook brand weight for loop strength. Avengers had similar mid-cycle attention spasms with no revenue conversion. the_read: Lethal Company is two years post-EA, sitting on $137.6M lifetime revenue and 18.8M owners, with a +16 breakout delta this week driven by 1.59M wishlists still on the board — that wishlist pool is the anomaly, not the live CCU.

the_read: Capcom's RE4 remake is twenty months post-launch at 7.6M owners and $133M lifetime gross on Steam alone — the +15 breakout delta this week is a creator-led second wave signature, not a new product story. Stream count quadrupling 20 to 81 on a stable 430 CCU base mirrors the Pacific Drive month-15 pattern almost exactly.

The 2.0M wishlist tail on a launched product is the number to stare at — that is a discount-conversion reservoir, not intent for a future release. At $39.99 with a 97% positive rating across 249K reviews, the next seasonal sale is a near-deterministic revenue event for Capcom's PC P&L.
Worth flagging: revenue 7d delta of +0.1% confirms this is an attention spike preceding monetization, not concurrent with it. Classic lag pattern on premium SKUs above $30.
2050650.against_consensus: Consensus treats RE4 as a finished story — shipped, reviewed, banked. The contrarian read is that Capcom's back catalogue on PC behaves more like a recurring-revenue annuity than a packaged-goods release, and the market consistently under-models second-wave creator cascades on 18-month-old AAA remakes because the absolute CCU numbers stay modest.
2050650.comparable: Closest analogue is Pacific Drive's month-15 creator-led second wave — 180% Twitch hours week-over-week on a stable follower base, capturing roughly 30-50% of launch peak. RE4's stream count went 20 to 81, a 305% lift, but on a much larger installed base. The gap: Pacific Drive peaked at 23K CCU; RE4's projected second-wave CCU sits in the 1,000-6,000 band, roughly 4-20× smaller in concurrent terms but on 7.6M owners.
2050650.what_would_change_my_mind: If Twitch live viewers fail to clear 2,000 within three weeks while stream count holds above 80, the cascade is creator-supply-driven without audience pull and the revenue tail will not materialize.
risks: Premium $39.99 price point limits impulse conversion without a sale event.
Catalogue attention spikes often decay before Capcom's discount calendar catches them.

the_read: Tiny Glade has cleared $14.8M lifetime revenue at $14.99 with 1.31M owners and a 97% review score — a clean two-person-studio outcome that's already returned the four-year dev cycle many times over without a traditional publisher taking a cut.

The interesting number isn't the launch — it's the residual 1.75M wishlist tail. That's a larger unconverted reservoir than most cozy SKUs ever accumulate, suggesting Pounce Light is sitting on a discount-cycle annuity rather than a one-shot.

Live attention has collapsed to 10 Twitch viewers and 1 concurrent stream, which is fine: this was never a streamer-cascade title. The unit economics work because the audience is the non-gaming cozy buyer who finds it via algorithmic discovery and gifting, not via watch-time.
2198150.against_consensus: Consensus treats Tiny Glade as a finished story — launched, peaked, moved on. The contrarian read is that a 1.75M wishlist overhang at fifteen months post-launch is not a dead reservoir; it's a deferred-purchase pipeline that converts on every seasonal sale. The Watch band understates the discount-cycle revenue this SKU will quietly print through 2026.
2198150.comparable: Stardew Valley is the structural analog — solo/micro-team, multi-year dev, non-gaming audience, durable tail. At fifteen months post-launch Stardew was already past 2M units and climbing toward its 95K peak CCU ceiling. Tiny Glade sits at 1.31M owners against that benchmark — a roughly 35% gap in unit terms, with no combat hook or multiplayer vector to close it.
2198150.what_would_change_my_mind: A content update or sandbox-export feature that pushes concurrent Twitch streams back above 50 sustained for a fortnight would reframe this from annuity to second-wave candidate.
risks: No content roadmap disclosed; wishlist tail decays without re-trigger.
Cozy cluster is now crowded; discount visibility competes with twenty similar SKUs.
2198150.pull_quote: A 1.75M wishlist overhang fifteen months in isn't a dead reservoir — it's a deferred-purchase pipeline that prints quietly on every seasonal sale.

the_read: Frostpunk 2 cleared 1M units and $27.2M lifetime gross at a $44.99 ASP roughly five months post-launch — respectable for a sequel sim, but the 75% positive review band is the commercial story: 11 bit converted only a fraction of a 2.1M wishlist stockpile, suggesting the design pivot from city-builder to society-sim cost them the casual half of the funnel.

Attention signals have collapsed to maintenance levels — 8 concurrent Twitch viewers, 2 active streams — which for a single-player narrative sim is expected but kills the streamer-cascade optionality entirely. Future revenue waves now depend on roadmap execution and discount ladders, not organic discovery.

Unit economics are the saving grace here. 11 bit self-publishes, owns the IP, and the Frostpunk 1 tail (still selling eight years on) plus This War of Mine give them a credible cohort-recurring-revenue argument. A $25M+ launch on a sub-$10M budget is a solid base hit; the question is whether DLC and a Game Pass-style deal extend the curve.
1601580.against_consensus: Consensus framed the mixed reviews as a launch wobble that patches would fix. Six months in, the 75% positive figure has barely moved, and CCU has decayed faster than Frostpunk 1's did at the equivalent point. The read is not that the game failed — it cleared a million units — but that the addressable ceiling is materially lower than the wishlist count implied, and the sequel premium did not compound.
1601580.comparable: Hades sits 49,000 peak CCU at its 1.0 moment with a 98% positive review band; Frostpunk 2 peaked around 27,000 CCU at launch with 75% positive. The gap is roughly 23 review points and a 1.8× CCU shortfall against a critical-phenom benchmark. Frostpunk 2 is not in that conversion category — it is a competent sequel that will earn out on IP strength rather than awards-led tailwind.
1601580.what_would_change_my_mind: A major expansion DLC lifting review sentiment above 85% recent-positive and pushing CCU back above 15,000 for a sustained two-week window would re-rate this from Watch to a genuine durable-sim thesis.
risks: Mixed reviews compound — sequel fatigue blocks DLC attach rates.
Console port window cannibalizes PC discount-wave revenue.
1601580.pull_quote: 11 bit converted only a fraction of a 2.1M wishlist stockpile — the design pivot cost them the casual half of the funnel.

the_read: Pacific Drive crossed 1.2M owners and $19.6M lifetime gross against 1.43M wishlists — a wishlist-to-owner conversion near 85% that is healthy but tells you the long tail is now the entire story, not launch.

Attention signals are functionally dead: 33 concurrent Twitch viewers across 2 streams, with the stream count halving week-over-week. This is a product that has fully exited the discovery layer and is running on organic search and sale-window spikes.

Where the math still works: 83% positive across 25.5K reviews on a $29.99 SKU with a single-player loop means Kepler can keep harvesting Steam sale visibility for years. Revenue delta of +0.1% week-on-week is the flat hum of a catalog title, not a breakout in motion.
1458140.against_consensus: Consensus filed Pacific Drive as a modest 2024 win and moved on. The contrarian read is that the 1.43M wishlist pool — most of which never converted — is a dormant asset, not a failure signal. At $29.99 with strong reviews, every Steam seasonal sale is a re-acquisition event. The ceiling is low; the floor is unusually durable for a debut studio.
1458140.comparable: Hades hit roughly 49K peak CCU at 1.0 and rode awards coverage into month-two retention on a narrative-forward loop. Pacific Drive's projected peak CCU band of 1,000–6,000 sits roughly 8–50x below that, and review volume of 25.5K is about 4x behind Hades' equivalent lifecycle point. The shape rhymes; the magnitude does not.
1458140.what_would_change_my_mind: A sustained content drop or roguelike-mode pivot that pushes concurrent Twitch viewership above 2,000 for two consecutive weeks would force a re-rate from Watch to genuine breakout candidate.
risks: Single-player survival has no replay flywheel at current cadence.
Attention signals decaying faster than wishlist pool can convert.
1458140.pull_quote: The ceiling is low; the floor is unusually durable for a debut studio.

the_read: Twitch is showing 2,563 concurrent viewers across 100 streams against $77 lifetime revenue and 15 estimated owners — a textbook attention-without-conversion split that screams paid creator activation or a brief novelty loop, not organic demand.

The intent stack does not corroborate: 2,200 wishlists, 41 Steam followers, 16 IGDB hypes. Wishlist-to-follower ratio of 54:1 is abnormally wide and suggests the wishlist count was banked pre-launch and is now stale rather than compounding.

Unit economics are the tell. At $6.99 with one review on file twelve months post-launch, the revenue line is flat at 0.0% week-over-week. Gacha-cluster headwind plus a sub-$10 SKU caps LTV before any cosmetic monetization can carry the P&L.
2767790.against_consensus: Twitch CCU of 2,500-plus on an indie usually triggers a breakout call. The contrarian read: this is a streamer-novelty spike on a 12-month-old SKU with one review and effectively zero revenue movement. Attention without a wishlist re-acceleration or follower inflow is a closed loop, not a cascade ignition.

Rockin' Racket's Twitch reading sits in a Watch band projecting 1K-6K CCU — a 30-to-200× gap to Lethal Company at the comparable cascade-onset point, and without the intent corroboration.
